title: Mullin Banks It at Deal, Spends It at Sandwich
title_candidates: Mullin Banks It at Deal, Spends It at Sandwich
The Sixteenth Will See You Now
Spoon to Silverware: Mullin by Two
The Reigning Spoon Holder Takes the Lot
theme: Capital and expenditure: Mullin won this Trophy on the two Kent links he had never handled before, banked nine points by Friday, and then spent almost all of it at Prince's — surviving by two because Alex Baker spent faster.
opening_hook: Open on Alex Baker on the 16th tee at Prince's on Sunday, two points and three pars from the Trophy, and the 10 that followed — then rewind to Deal, where the reigning Wooden Spoon holder had quietly banked the lot.
foreshadow: Mullin arrives as the reigning Wooden Spoon holder — a Spoon in each of the last three TEGs, four in all — with eight Jackets and two Trophies behind him.
Alex Baker's 10 at the 16th at Royal Cinque Ports in R1: note the hole number.
Jon Baker arrives as defending Trophy champion and back-to-back Jacket holder, a man with no Wooden Spoon anywhere on his record.
Mullin's cushion after R2 is nine points — bank the number.

headline_candidates: Deal With It: Mullin Banks 40 and Seven Shots of Improvement
Alex Baker Finds a 10 at the 16th, and Not for the Last Time
Two Open Championships, and a Nine at the Third
rounds.chosen_headline: Deal With It: Mullin Banks 40 and Seven Shots of Improvement
rounds.angle: The reigning Spoon holder opens with the best round in the field — 40 points, 87 gross, seven better than his TEG 13 visit — while Alex Baker plants the tournament's motif with a 10 at the 16th and Gregg Williams takes a nine at the third.

headline_candidates: Mullin 41, and the Lead Becomes a Cushion
Twelve Shots in Four Holes: Littlestone Presents Its Bill
Romney Marsh Remembers Jon Baker's 79. Jon Baker Does Not.
rounds.chosen_headline: Mullin 41, and the Lead Becomes a Cushion
rounds.angle: A second best-in-field round (41 points, 85 gross, seven better than last visit) stretches the lead to nine, while Alex Baker bleeds twelve shots in four holes and Jon Baker comes home thirteen worse than the 79 he posted here in TEG 13.

headline_candidates: A Nine at the Eighth, and a Lead That Barely Notices
Williams Answers 27 With 39; Nobody Sees It
rounds.chosen_headline: A Nine at the Eighth, and a Lead That Barely Notices
rounds.angle: Mullin's first bottom-half round — 36 points, a nine at the eighth — is rescued by thirteen points in the last four holes; Gregg Williams follows a 27 with a 39 and a Prince's personal best of 86; Jon Baker's 28 pins him to the bottom.

headline_candidates: The Sixteenth Will See You Now
A Course Record and a Wooden Spoon, Same Man, Same Afternoon
Mullin Loses the Round, Wins Everything Else
rounds.chosen_headline: The Sixteenth Will See You Now
rounds.angle: Alex Baker outscores the leader by six and closes nine to two, then makes 10 at the 16th — stroke index 17, the easiest hole on the card; Jon Baker breaks the Prince's record with 83 and ties the all-time birdie-streak record and still takes the Spoon; Mullin's 37, quad at the 10th and all, is exactly enough.

players.arc: Reigning Wooden Spoon holder with four Spoons and eight Jackets behind him: posts the two best rounds in the field at Deal and Littlestone with personal bests at both, then two bottom-half rounds at Prince's, and still walks off with the Trophy on 154 and the Jacket at +68.
Outscored the champion in two of the four rounds and lost by two, with twelve shots bled in four holes at Littlestone and two 10s at a 16th hole as the itemised receipt.

Defending Trophy champion with no Spoon on his record: thirteen worse than his 79 at Littlestone, last in the field twice, then a course-record 83 and a record-tying pair of birdies on the final day — and the Wooden Spoon by twelve.
Quietly posted a personal-best gross total of +76 with new personal bests at Royal Cinque Ports and Prince's, swung 27 to 39 between R2 and R3, and was never once in the Trophy conversation.

venue_notes: TEG's 2nd visit to Kent, and four rounds of pure links: Royal Cinque Ports and Littlestone each for the 2nd TEG round, Prince's Shore/Dunes for the 2nd and 3rd. Frame Deal as the formidable Open venue where the Trophy was actually banked, and Prince's as the place it was nearly given back. Every player had a TEG 13 number here to be measured against — use those deltas rather than generic wind talk.
course_history_notes: David Mullin set a new personal best at all three Kent courses: 87 at Royal Cinque Ports (7 better), 85 at Littlestone (7 better), 91 at Prince's (1 better).
Jon Baker was 13 shots worse than his last visit to Littlestone, where his prior best was 79 gross (TEG 13), and 7 worse at Royal Cinque Ports — before a new personal best of 83 at Prince's in R4.
Gregg Williams was 11 shots worse than his last visit to Littlestone, but posted new personal bests at Prince's (86 in R3) and Royal Cinque Ports (93 in R1).
Alex Baker's new personal best at Royal Cinque Ports in R1 — 98 gross, 4 better — and 5 shots worse than his last visit to Prince's.

trophy_storyline.subject: David Mullin's Trophy: banked at Deal and Littlestone, then defended with his fingernails at Prince's
trophy_storyline.why_it_matters: The man who had taken the Wooden Spoon in each of the last three TEGs won the main event, and won it in the first two rounds rather than the last two.
trophy_storyline.shape: Setup: two best-in-field rounds, 40 at Royal Cinque Ports and 41 at Littlestone, with personal bests on both links, open a nine-point lead by Friday evening. Turn: Prince's takes it straight back — 36 and 37, bottom half of the field both days, a nine at the eighth and an eight at the tenth — while Alex Baker charges and closes nine to two. Resolution: the margin holds at two because Alex Baker's own final round detonated at the 16th; Mullin was the man still standing there to collect.

jacket_storyline.subject: The Green Jacket: +68, and settled before Prince's ever got a say
jacket_storyline.why_it_matters: Mullin's Jacket was the one competition genuinely built rather than inherited — he beat Jon Baker head-to-head in three of the four rounds and was twelve clear after R2.
jacket_storyline.shape: Setup: 87 at Deal and 85 at Littlestone, both personal bests, put Mullin twelve clear of Jon Baker by Friday. Turn: Jon Baker's final-round 83 — a new Prince's course record — claws the deficit from fifteen at its worst down to seven. Resolution: too late by two rounds; Mullin closes at +68 by seven, and even Jon Baker's best day of the tournament could not have flipped it.

spoon_storyline.subject: Jon Baker's Wooden Spoon: the defending champion who set a course record on his way to last place
spoon_storyline.why_it_matters: The reigning Trophy holder, back-to-back Jacket winner and a man with no Spoon anywhere on his record finished twelve adrift of the next worst — and did it while breaking a course record.
spoon_storyline.shape: Setup: bottom of the Spoon race from the fourth hole of R1 and never off it, with 29, 29 and 28 and a Littlestone round thirteen shots worse than the 79 he posted there in TEG 13. Turn: on the final day he plays the best golf of anyone — back-to-back birdies at the 12th and 13th that tie the all-time TEG birdie-streak record, 39 points, and an 83 that is a new Prince's course record. Resolution: he still takes the Spoon on 125, twelve behind Gregg Williams, and rounds it off with a quadruple-bogey eight at the last, which is the sort of punctuation the record book deserves.

discovered_storylines.subject: Alex Baker's four-round audit of the blow-up hole
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: He lost the Trophy by two points having outscored the champion in two rounds — every point of that margin is traceable to a small number of catastrophic holes, itemised across all four days.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: a 10 at the 16th and an eight at the 11th at Royal Cinque Ports, then twelve shots bled in four holes at Littlestone including a nine at the fifth and an eight at the eighth. Turn: he keeps arriving anyway — an eight at the tenth at Prince's on Saturday, then a final round that goes 10 points in the opening three holes and 11 more from the 13th to the 15th, closing him to within two. Resolution: a 10 at the 16th, stroke index 17, the easiest hole on the card, and the audit balances at exactly two points short.

discovered_storylines.subject: Gregg Williams's best golf, played entirely offstage
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: He posted a personal-best gross total and two new course personal bests in a tournament where nobody once mentioned his name in a competition.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: a nine at the third at Deal, then a 27 at Littlestone, eleven shots worse than his previous visit — a man apparently heading for the Spoon conversation. Turn: 39 points and an 86 at Prince's on Saturday, a new personal best there, with nine points in three holes from the 9th before a triple bogey at the 12th ends it. Resolution: a personal-best gross total of +76, having trailed the Jacket by eighteen at one stage and closed to eight, and a finish of third with nothing whatsoever to show for it.

payoffs.seed: Mullin the reigning Wooden Spoon holder, three in a row
payoffs.payoff: He takes the Trophy on 154 and the Jacket at +68 in the same TEG (b02, b08) — the previous loser elevated, comprehensively.

payoffs.seed: Alex Baker's 10 at the 16th at Royal Cinque Ports (R1)
payoffs.payoff: A second 10 at a 16th (b01), this one on stroke index 17, three holes from the Trophy, losing it by two.

payoffs.seed: Jon Baker has never been last
payoffs.resolves_in: How the three were decided — the Spoon
payoffs.payoff: He collects it on 125 points, twelve adrift (b32), on the same afternoon he sets the Prince's course record (cr01) and ties the all-time birdie-streak record (sr01).
Outscored in both Prince's rounds, Mullin finishes with exactly two of the nine still in hand (b20).

vehicle_fit_response.note: The Spoon-holder-turned-champion material is real and gets full prominence, but `inversion` carries it better because it also holds the other half — the defending Trophy champion taking his first Spoon — and the close finish (final margin 2) mandates `counterfactual` as the frame.

why_the_champion_won: He banked it early — best-in-field 40 and 41 with personal bests on two links he had never handled — and then held on through two bottom-half rounds at Prince's while Alex Baker, who outscored him over both of them and could have won with merely an ordinary round instead of his worst, gave back more at the 16th than he had managed to take.
